name: Diego Ramirez
about_me: I'm Diego, founder of SoilSense, a low-cost soil-moisture sensor for urban farms, based in Detroit. We have 40 sensors deployed with community gardens. I'm raising a $600k pre-seed and looking for climate or ag investors who back hardware.
goals: Close a $600k pre-seed round for SoilSense
Find two more urban-farm pilot partners

debriefs.text: Met Julia Brennan at the Eastern Market grower meeting. She runs Grown Together Detroit, a network of 30 community gardens, and wants soil sensors in every plot by spring. She offered to connect us with five garden leads.

Pitched Priya Rao, partner at Northwind Climate Fund, at Detroit Hardware Night. She said they back climate hardware at seed and wants to see unit economics on the sensor. I promised to send her our cost-down plan next week.

Coffee with Elena Ortiz, program officer at the Great Lakes Innovation Fund. The fund gives state grants up to $100k for clean-tech pilots and the next deadline is January 10. She said ag sensing fits.
Talked to Omar Haddad, founder of GridLeaf. He's raising his seed round too and said Priya was the first check he got a meeting with. He knows Jamal Pierce well.
Met Derek Olsen, a patent attorney at a Detroit firm, at the Launchpad open house. He offers a free first consult to student and early founders. I want to ask him about our probe design.
Chatted with Victor Stahl from Lakeshore Capital in Chicago. He said they're not doing climate this year, only consumer and fintech, but he'd look again at Series A.
